clue.text: Child uses it to scatter toys

definitions.note: a nursery word for a foot, the kind of word a small child uses

indicators.note: to scatter the words around it is to throw their letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A small child makes a mess by flinging playthings across the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' seems to point at the toys, but 'Child uses it' is the whole definition: a word from the nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery word for a foot, used by or to small children.

clue.text: Cricketer keeps note — he has to watch the score

definitions.text: he has to watch the score

indicators.note: keeps means the cricketer's name holds the note inside it

parts.note: Victor Trumper was a famous Australian batsman
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A cricketer holds on to a message while keeping an eye on the scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' suggests cricket runs; it is a musical score that a brass player in an orchestra must follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass player reads music from the score while performing.

clue.text: Old banger, perhaps — one with an original instrument

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old, battered car
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: original in the sense of novel, so the two letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old jalopy, perhaps one with an unusual musical device inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a decrepit car (also a sausage or firework).
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Easter confectionery from Lambert's father?

parts.note: Lambert Simnel was a Tudor pretender whose father, legend says, was a baker who made this Easter treat

explanation.surface: A Tudor pretender's father bakes a seasonal treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambert Simnel claimed the English throne in 1487; folk etymology makes his father the baker of this fruit cake eaten at Easter in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich fruit cake topped with marzipan, eaten in Britain at Easter and on Mothering Sunday.

clue.text: Snake annoyed and beginning to hiss

definitions.note: the word hiss begins with the breathy sound of H, the noun sense of the answer

parts.note: an asp is a venomous Egyptian snake
irate means angry, annoyed

explanation.surface: An irritated serpent starts hissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to hiss' looks like more wordplay, but it is the definition: the H at the start of 'hiss' is a breathed sound, which phoneticians call by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetics names the breathy H sound this way, and H is the opening sound of hiss.

clue.text: Girl will angle for lobster

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl
'll is the contraction of will
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A girl intends to go angling for a lobster.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster is an example of a sea creature with a hard outer case.

clue.text: Terrorists new to the country

parts.note: the IRA was the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: Terrorists turn up fresh in a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a Middle Eastern nation.

clue.text: Doing damage to railing

explanation.surface: Someone harms a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Harming or misusing something; and berating or reviling someone.

clue.text: The other side is concealed in Yemen

indicators.note: the letters are concealed in a jumbled form within the country name

explanation.surface: Rebels are hiding out in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Your opponent in a war or game is the hostile party.

clue.text: Wheeze a bit astride a nag

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase astride a nag is taken, the letters spanning its words

explanation.surface: A horse-riding trick, sitting with legs either side of an old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheeze' is British slang for a clever scheme or plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze is a bright plan or notion.

clue.text: Not equipped for hand-to-hand fighting

explanation.surface: A soldier lacks the kit for close combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Without weapons, and the term in 'unarmed combat', fighting body to body without arms.

clue.text: Removal of safe on a cycle

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: an era is a long period or cycle of time
sure means safe, certain

explanation.surface: A safe is moved about on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' looks like a strongbox but is an adjective, and 'a cycle' suggests a bicycle rather than a span of time; 'on' places the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing out or deleting something is its removal.

clue.text: From the very beginning, demure girl students start to yawn

parts.note: prim means demure, prudish
Eva is a girl's name
L is a learner; two Ls are students

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of yawn

explanation.surface: A shy girl at college begins to yawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval means belonging to the earliest age, so the adverb means since the very first times.

clue.text: Orderly is pretty good

explanation.surface: An orderly in hospital is rather good at the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and well kept; and fairly large or decent, as in a sizeable sum of money.

clue.text: Pearl River swapping places with Eliza, say

indicators.note: swapping places tells you to put the second piece first and the first second

parts.note: a river is cryptically a flower, something that flows
Pearl is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Pearl River changes places with Eliza, perhaps as a theatrical role.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle in Shaw's Pygmalion sells blooms in Covent Garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion and My Fair Lady sells blooms on the street.

clue.text: Instalment of money puts Henry in ecstasy

indicators.note: in places the letter for Henry inside the word for ecstasy

parts.note: a trance is a state of rapture or ecstasy
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Getting a payment sends Henry into raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice of a payment or loan.

clue.text: One character in the serial has to die during a festival

indicators.note: during means the word for die sits inside the festival

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival
to end is to die

explanation.surface: A soap opera character is killed off over the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running British TV soap opera set in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the East End of London, or a character in that soap.

clue.text: Banned, for example, in two states

indicators.note: in places the example abbreviation inside the two state abbreviations

parts.note: Ill. is the abbreviation for Illinois
AL is the abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: Something prohibited, say, in a couple of American states.
explanation.definitionFit: Something against the law is forbidden or prohibited.

clue.text: You may be taken in by these symbols of emancipation

definitions.text: You may be taken in by these symbols of emancipation

parts.words: You may be taken in by these symbols of emancipation
parts.note: keys that let you into a house, seen as tokens of a young person's freedom to come and go

explanation.surface: Symbols of liberation may deceive you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' seems to mean fooled, but it means let into the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Front-door keys given to a young person mark their freedom to come home when they like.

clue.text: Changes suit, having another

parts.note: in card games, failing to follow the suit led although holding a card of that suit

explanation.surface: Someone changes clothes even though they own a spare.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clothes; in bridge or whist, playing a different suit when you could have followed is a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: The card-game term for failing to follow suit while holding a card that could.

clue.text: The land of the Dong

parts.note: the dong is the currency of a south-east Asian country, echoing Lear's nonsense poem The Dong with a Luminous Nose

explanation.surface: A nonsense-poem setting: the home of Lear's creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The dong is the currency unit of this Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: This south-east Asian nation uses the dong as its money.

clue.text: Crook with OBE, nevertheless

indicators.note: to crook is to bend, so the letters are bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: A villain has been given an honour all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a noun (a criminal), but it signals bending the letters of WITH OBE; OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning however or all the same.

clue.text: Half-way line for the Harlem Globetrotters?

definitions.text: Half-way line for the Harlem Globetrotters?

parts.words: Half-way line for the Harlem Globetrotters?
parts.note: people who trot round the globe would have as their half-way line the circle around its middle

explanation.surface: Where the touring basketball team draws its midcourt line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Harlem Globetrotters are a touring basketball team; read literally, globe-trotters' mid-line is the one round the Earth's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary line round the Earth halfway between the poles.

clue.text: Hesitate, as Miss Doolittle would, to swear

indicators.note: Eliza Doolittle, the Cockney of Pygmalion, drops her aitches, so the H goes

parts.note: to haver is to hesitate or dither

explanation.surface: A speaker hesitates, Cockney style, before making an oath.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare firmly, to state as true.

clue.text: Murderer of Agamemnon, so lacking protection

indicators.note: lacking means the word for so is taken away

parts.note: Aegisthus killed Agamemnon in Greek myth, with Clytemnestra
thus means so

explanation.surface: The man who killed Agamemnon was therefore without defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronage or shelter, originally the shield of Zeus.

clue.text: Material is sheer and ought to become transparent

indicators.note: the letters are made to become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fabric that is gauzy should be clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheer' and 'ought' sound like plain description of the material; their ten letters rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear enough to see through, as thin fabric is.

clue.text: Employment tax

explanation.surface: A job attracts tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work or job; and to burden or strain, as tax does.

clue.text: Mountain above source of holy river

indicators.note: in a down clue above means the mountain comes before the next piece

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, here of holy

explanation.surface: A mountain stands over the spring of a sacred river.
explanation.walkthrough: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's Kubla Khan names this sacred stream flowing through Xanadu.

clue.text: Having broken in horse, he came first

parts.note: a gent is a man, one referred to as he
led means came first, was in front

explanation.surface: A rider tamed a horse and won the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To gentle a horse is to tame or train it, so this past tense says it was tamed.

clue.text: One could well be bowled over by a cheese

definitions.text: One could well be bowled over by a cheese

parts.words: One could well be bowled over by a cheese
parts.note: in the old game of pins, the flat disc thrown at them is called a cheese

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished by a lump of cheddar.
explanation.walkthrough: In the old English game of pins, the thrown disc is called a cheese; 'bowled over' means knocked down, not amazed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin knocked down in the bowling game, which may be hit by the thrown disc called a cheese.

clue.text: A representative in Hants, say, found on the cliffs

indicators.note: in places A and the representative inside the county word

parts.note: Hants (Hampshire) is an English county, a shire
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament from Hampshire is spotted on a coastal clifftop.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock samphire is a fleshy plant growing on sea cliffs.

clue.text: Burns in trousers

explanation.surface: Someone gets scorched inside their trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Blazes up suddenly; and wide-bottomed slacks fashionable in the 1970s.
